blocks.content: Read the question stem twice to identify whether it asks for correct or incorrect options.

rows: Which of the following is NOT correct?
Circle or highlight 'NOT' immediately before reading options.
Speed given in km/h while time is given in seconds.
Convert all parameters into unified SI units first.
Statement uses absolute terms like 'Always' or 'Only'.
Treat extreme statements with skepticism unless factually backed.

items: Negation traps ('Which of the following is NOT correct?') account for a high percentage of avoidable negative marks.
Option 'A' is frequently designed as a partial distractor to trick rushed candidates.
Watch for subtle word changes in static GK and polity questions that alter the legal or historical meaning completely.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Always verify measurement units (e.g., converting km/h to m/s) before starting calculations.
Identify negation keywords like 'NOT', 'EXCEPT', or 'INCORRECT' in the question stem.
Be skeptical of extreme qualifiers such as 'Always', 'Never', 'All', or 'Only' in option statements.
Verify that all conditions in multi-statement questions are completely satisfied before choosing the final option.
